data.content_ref: inline:{"analogy":{"adopted_commitment_refs":[],"disanalogies":["A placebo checklist replaces the entire instrument; an adversarial case-set replaces the evaluation items while keeping the instrument fixed.","Placebo effects are subject-centered; adversarial case-sets are stimulus-centered.","A placebo checklist tests the panel; an adversarial case-set tests the checklist."],"overturn_conditions":["If the checklist cues are provably necessary and sufficient for the outcome, the adversarial set cannot be constructed and the test is vacuous.","If the panel's accuracy on the adversarial set is high but only because it ignores the checklist on hard cases, the test misattributes the gain to the checklist rather than to extra-checklist judgment."],"shared_structure":["Both adversarial case-sets and placebo checklists create a dissociation between a surface procedure and a target outcome.","Both rely on breaking a spurious correlation to reveal whether the underlying mechanism is genuinely tracking the target.","Both require the outcome to be objectively measurable to serve as the ground truth for the dissociation."],"source_memory_refs":["SCR_001","SRC_002","SRC_008"],"transfer_claims":["The logic of adversarial evaluation in machine learning transfers: one can probe a model's reliance on spurious features by constructing inputs where those features are flipped relative to the label.","The concept of 'shortcut learning' transfers: a checklist may teach shortcuts to the correct answer that fail on out-of-distribution cases.","The requirement for a held-out adversarial set transfers: if the panel has seen the decorrelated cases during training, the test is contaminated."]},"claim":"For tasks with objectively verifiable outcomes, a single evaluation can distinguish genuine reliability gain from mere checklist compliance by constructing an adversarial case-set in which checklist-compliance and the correct outcome are decorrelated. If the panel maintains high accuracy on this decorrelated set, it demonstrates genuine task-discrimination; if its accuracy collapses, the original gain was compliance-tracking.","counterconditions":[{"case":"If the outcome is a deterministic function of the checklist cues, it is impossible to decorrelate them by construction, and the test cannot be performed within a single evaluation.","checker_spec":null,"eval":"observation"},{"case":"If the panel uses non-checklist contextual information to adjust its scores, the decorrelation test may attribute survival to the checklist when it was actually extra-checklist judgment.","checker_spec":null,"eval":"observation"},{"case":"If the adversarial case-set is not representative of the panel's intended deployment domain, the test has low ecological validity.","checker_spec":null,"eval":"observation"}],"definitions":[],"derivation":[],"formalization_refs":[],"mechanism":"Mere compliance means the panel's judgment is driven by surface features of the checklist that usually correlate with the outcome but are not causally necessary. An adversarial case-set breaks that correlation: cases are selected where high checklist-scores coexist with low-probability outcomes and vice versa. This is a stress test of the internal validity of each checklist item. If the panel's accuracy survives the decorrelation, its judgment is not solely driven by the checklist's surface cues but by a deeper mapping to the outcome. If it fails, the checklist was acting as a mere proxy.","premises":[],"schema":"deepreason-reasoning-envelope-v1","scope":{"covers":[],"excludes":[]},"simulation_refs":[],"uncertainties":[]}
